subject: Re: StratusWorks webhook 503 spikes — escalation & SLA commitments
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@stratusworks.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: platform-ops@stratusworks.com
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Integration: intermittent 503s on webhook /batch inference - urgent

Hi Soojin,

We started seeing intermittent 503s from Redwood’s webhook endpoint (POST /v1/infer) starting ~08:50 PT this morning. Impact: our ingest pipeline is backing up and causing delayed batches to be retried twice. We are seeing ~12% error rate on requests that normally succeed. This is affecting our nightly job and impacts customers in EMEA.

I attached a brief sample of request IDs and timestamps. Can someone on your side confirm whether this looks like a capacity spike, routing flap, or a model-side rejection? Our platform team is standing by. We need:
- Immediate triage/confirmation of the root cause (routing / capacity / model)
- Estimated time to stabilization or mitigation steps we can take (e.g., fallback to smaller model variant)
- A note on whether this counts as a breach against the 99.5% webhook availability in our integration SLA (we're tracking incident metrics on our side)

Requesting an initial reply within 30 minutes if possible.

Thanks,
Elena
Engineering Lead, Integrations
StratusWorks
[Attachment: sample-reqids-20260628.csv (text/csv)]

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@stratusworks.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Integration: intermittent 503s on webhook /batch inference - urgent

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and the sample file. Sorry for the disruption.

Quick status from our side:
- I’ve looped in Jordan (Platform Engineering) and Marissa (Partner Success) to coordinate the response.
- Jordan is looking at the request trace IDs now; initial checks show queueing on one dedicated pool and a small number of OOM restarts on a worker group that serves the v1/infer path.

Immediate asks from us:
1) Can you send a 15–30 minute window with high-fidelity traces (request body + headers) for 3–5 failed requests so Jordan can reproduce locally?
2) Please confirm whether you have a runbook to temporarily route heavy batch traffic to an alternate Redwood endpoint (we can provide a migration token if needed).

Proposed immediate mitigations:
- We will enable a temporary model variant (smaller instance/quantized) for your partner pool to reduce memory pressure — Jordan can roll this out in the next 30 minutes if you approve.
- If you prefer, we can enable per-request retries with jitter on our ingress for 503s for the next 4 hours while we remediate.

Marissa — can you advise on SLA language and whether we should pre-authorize a credits packet if this ends up being an SLA breach?

I’ll keep you posted.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none]

Hi Elena / Ben — I’m jumping in on the SLA side. Thank you for the logs — that helped. Key notes: 

- We are authorizing an immediate model-variant roll to a 8-bit quantized smaller instance for your partner pool; Jordan will execute and validate. We will mark this as a "mitigation step" (non-permanent).
- We will also enable egress retries with exponential backoff for 503 responses for a 6-hour window while we fully remediate.
- Regarding the SLA: with the current numbers you shared (99.42% over 7 days), we will open an incident review. If our postmortem determines the outage is within our control and an SLA breach, we will offer a one-time service credit consistent with our partner terms.

Action items & owners:
- Jordan: roll & validate quantized variant on partner pool (ETA 30–45m).
- Soojin: coordinate comms to StratusWorks exec sponsor; track any downstream customer impact.
- Marissa: prepare credit pre-approval package (internal) in case breach confirmed.
- Elena/Ben: confirm when you switch traffic to new endpoint (if you take that route) so we can observe.

Marissa Cole
Director, Partner Success
Redwood Inference

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@stratusworks.com>, Benjamin Torres <benjamin.torres@stratusworks.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Integration: intermittent 503s on webhook /batch inference - urgent

Hi team — quick post-action update and next steps following the mitigation window.

What we observed:
- Memory pressure on an older worker group caused sporadic OOM restarts; this correlated with larger batch payloads from StratusWorks between ~08:45–10:15 PT on 2026-06-28. The restarts caused a surge of 503 responses while the autoscaler rebalanced.
- The quantized variant reduced memory footprint and dropped 503s to <0.5% during the mitigation window.

Permanent remediation plan (next 7 days):
1) Upgrade the affected worker group to a +2GB instance class and tighten autoscale thresholds (Owner: Jordan) — ETA 72 hours for rollout and validation.
2) Add request-size gating at the partner ingress with a soft-fail path and clear 413/422 responses we can map to retries (Owner: StratusWorks platform team) — we’ll share a suggested gating policy.
3) Joint postmortem on Fri 07/02 @ 10:00 PT — owners: Jordan (Redwood), Ben (StratusWorks), Soojin (partnership comms), Marissa (credits/partner ops).

SLA note: based on our initial internal analysis, we will not pre-emptively issue credits. We will complete the joint postmortem and apply the SLA calculation window and hit/miss rules defined in section 4.2 of the SLO excerpt. Marissa will provide a formal determination within 5 business days after the postmortem.

Attachments: postmortem-ask-template.docx (please fill the impact & timeline sections before the call).

Thanks for the quick collaboration here — Jordan
Senior Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: postmortem-ask-template.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]
